subject: Pilot proposal: model fit + JSON-schema toolcall qualification for transaction-vetting
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbusfin.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot proposal: model fit + JSON-schema toolcall qualification for transaction-vetting

Hi Aisha / Ravi —

Great speaking with you today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear pilot scope: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Client goal: automated first-pass transaction vetting to flag high-risk entries for manual review.
- Inputs: free-text memos + structured transaction fields from your ingestion pipeline.
- Outputs: structured verdict (allow/flag/reject), risk_score (0-100), and a short rationale string. Must be JSON-schema compliant for downstream ingestion.

Redwood pilot proposal (3-week scope)
1) Model fit + baseline evaluation (week 1): run two candidate open models on a 5k-sample slice you provide. We'll produce token-cost/latency/accuracy tradeoffs and a recommended quantized variant.
2) Structured-output & tool/function calling test (week 2): validate JSON Schema compliance for the output shape, and exercise function-calling for lookups (e.g., attendee->sanctions check).
3) Regression & retry plan (week 3): define quality regression thresholds on your prompt set and a retry/backoff strategy when schema validation fails.

Immediate asks from your side
- Share a 5k anonymized sample (CSV or NDJSON) and the target JSON schema. If NDJSON is easier, we can consume directly.
- Confirm success criteria: preferred precision on 'flag' class and max avg latency SLO.

I've attached a draft prompt set (nimbus_eval_promptset_v1.json) and our suggested schema (schema_transaction_v2.json). Also linking an internal benchmark so you can preview expected performance for similar workloads: https://redwood-internal.s3/benchmarks/nimbus/2028-q3

Next meeting: propose Wed 10/11 10am PT for a 30-minute alignment and to review the sample load.

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: nimbus_eval_promptset_v1.json (application/json), schema_transaction_v2.json (application/json)
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbusfin.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@nimbusfin.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2028 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal: model fit + JSON-schema toolcall qualification for transaction-vetting

Thanks, Olga — good summary. Two quick clarifications: 

1) Sample: we'll provide 5k rows but only 500 will be labelled for "flag"/"allow" to start — is that sufficient for a baseline?
2) Schema: our downstream pipeline expects a strict key ordering for ingestion (transaction_id, verdict, risk_score, rationale). Can you guarantee schema ordering or do we need a shim?

Also, our compliance team asked about PII handling — we can anonymize memos but want to confirm Redwood's retention policy for pilot data.

Aisha
Head of Risk Engineering | Nimbus Financial
aisha.khan@nimbusfin.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: FWD: Pilot proposal + Nimbus clarifications (label counts + schema ordering)

Team — forwarding Nimbus' clarifying questions. Key asks:
- 500 labelled positives for "flag" (they can provide more later) — can we run a useful baseline at that label density?
- They require strict key ordering in the JSON output. They asked whether Redwood can guarantee ordering or if we should provide a lightweight ingestion shim.
- Compliance / retention: they want confirmation on pilot data retention and anonymization steps.

Proposed answers and action items:
1) Baseline with 500 labels: we can still compute precision/recall and provide bootstrapped confidence intervals. We'll be explicit about label variance and recommend at least +1k labelled examples for stable estimates on the "flag" class. (Marcus: can you include a short note about statistical variance and a suggested sampling plan?)

2) JSON ordering: our function-calling + structured output path currently validates schema via JSON Schema (draft-07) and returns objects. Most JSON parsers don't enforce key order; however, we can return a canonicalized string or provide ordered keys in the top-level response to satisfy their ingestion. Options: (a) Redwood returns an ordered JSON string field 'ordered_payload' alongside the object; (b) we provide a tiny shim (lambda) that reorders keys before pushing into their pipeline. Which is lower ops?

3) Retention: default pilot retention is 30 days on hosted endpoints, with options for shorter retention and per-project KMS. (Laura: can you draft a two-line blurb for compliance with retention+anonymization options we can send to them?)

Attachments included for their review in my first email. I'm proposing to confirm Wed 10/11 10am PT.

Olga

On Mon, Oct 9, 2028 at 3:02 PM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message included)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Pilot proposal + Nimbus clarifications (label counts + schema ordering)

Quick notes from the infra/serving side: 

On baseline with 500 positives
- Statistically: 500 labelled positives can give an initial signal but confidence intervals will be wide for per-class precision. We should report bootstrap CI and per-pattern buckets (e.g., memo-length, channel) to show variance. Recommend they provide an additional 1k labelled cases if they aim for production calibration.

On key ordering and schema validation
- We don't rely on key order for internal correctness. For strict ordering requirement we can: 
  * Implement server-side canonicalization: after generating the output object we serialize using an ordered key list (transaction_id, verdict, risk_score, rationale) and return the string in a field ordered_payload. Minimal change to runtime and zero infra on their side.
  * Alternatively, we can deliver a small Cloud Function (their cloud or ours) to transform the object before ingest.
- I'll prototype canonicalization today (JIRA INF-9812) and attach a small code snippet and unit test. We should also add a schema-validation retry policy: 
  * On schema validation failure: 1 immediate retry with temperature adjust (0.0) and deterministic sampling, then flag to manual review if still failing.

On retention/PII
- We support per-project retention settings. Default hosted pilot retention: 30 days; can be shortened to 7 days for compliance. We do not persist raw memos beyond retention window; anonymization should be done client-side. We'll provide a retention statement for the compliance team.

I'll add the benchmark csv (redwood-benchmark-2028-q3.csv) with baseline latency/cost numbers for candidate models (open-llama-34b, redwood-compat-13b-quant) and share the prototype for ordered_payload.

—Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Hi Aisha / Ravi —

Thanks for the quick reply and for confirming labels. Follow-up items ahead of Wed's sync: 

1) Data share (action: Nimbus) — please upload the 5k anonymized sample to the secure link or drop in the SFTP by EOD Tue. We need the NDJSON preferred format.
2) Redwood deliverables (action: Redwood) — Marcus will prototype ordered_payload canonicalization and include unit tests (JIRA INF-9812). We'll provide the first runbench (redwood-benchmark-2028-q3.csv) and a recommended model candidate (open-llama-34b quantized) with expected median latency ~92ms/token on our dedicated pool.
3) Compliance (action: Redwood / Nimbus) — Laura will email a short retention/anonymization statement; default pilot retention is 30 days but we can reduce to 7 days per request.

Meeting confirmed: Wed 11 Oct, 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent). Agenda: sample format + success criteria + timeline for labelled augmentation.

If you want, we're happy to spin a sandbox endpoint so you can exercise JSON-schema validation and retries against a subset before the full run.

Best,
Olga
